title: Poisson Limit Experiments for Growing Multivariate Exponential Tilts at Support Boundaries
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier subfield below field floor; not salvageable within scope. Math panel returned revise with unresolved geometry premise and dependency findings, so mathematical soundness is not established.
gap_reasons: The note proves geometry-specific all-tilt minimax rates, fixed-density local Poisson equivalence, and an asymptotic decision-value characterization, but it does not deliver an instantiated full-profile certificate, numerical bracket, or decoded critical-regime rule.

The claimed finite-sample honest transfer is not fully reproducible because the proof merely names a combined deterministic error bound d_n and a sufficiently slow certificate resolution without explicitly computing all finite-n target, nuisance, rounding, and coverage corrections.

Tangent coordinates are shown to help only on a constructed two-profile subexperiment; whether they improve the full-profile minimax values remains open, so the paper does not establish the broader tangent-information frontier.

The proof says the disk window W=[1,2]×[-1,1] is contained in int(E_disk), but (1,1) and (1,-1) lie on ∂E_disk (s=z²/2); replace that false premise with the direct eventual inclusion W⊂E_{D,t} (which does hold for sufficiently large t) and carry its threshold in the quantitative ledger.

Its displayed proof invokes p_x≥p_0 to remove empty strata, but ass:stratum-mass is absent from depends_on; either add that dependency/model-class condition or reproduce the expansion with zero-mass strata excluded and no p_0 invocation.
proof_attempt_summary: Three proposal drafts led to a field-tier Stage -0.5 acceptance, followed by a D0 graph with all-tilt rate bounds, a fixed-density marked-Poisson experiment, finite-program value claims, and an asymptotic transfer argument. Stage 0.5 judged the delivered package subfield because it lacked an instantiated full-profile certificate and fully computed finite-sample coverage ledger; the math panel also left two proof/dependency defects unresolved. This archive is a research attempt, not a soundness-certified result; future work should repair the listed defects and re-anchor the novelty claim before reuse.
tldr: Multivariate exponential tilts concentrate observations at a smooth exposed boundary of a disk or at a corner of a square. The global minimax rate is governed by the resulting effective boundary count, but at the critical count a Gaussian influence-function calculation no longer determines optimal inference. For the explicitly one-stratum family \(P_{n,f,g}\) with fixed nuisance density \(f\), the core result constructs the geometry-specific Bernoulli-marked Poisson experiment, certifies its exact full-profile squared-risk and connected-interval values by convergent finite rational programs, and transfers decoded rules to data-only local procedures after estimating \(f(a_D^\star)\). The generic finite-game certificate scaffold is not itself the novelty; the advance is the marked geometry, tangent information, and certified nuisance-aware two-way transfer. Growing-tilt and convergent finite-tilt Gaussian limits are stated separately, and a full-box comparison of tangent-aware and distance-only experiments remains the first-class open question.
gap: Existing multivariate tilt theory is finite-tilt and Gaussian, scalar growing-tilt theory stops at rates and Gaussian limits, and general experiment-comparison or confidence-game machinery, including the in-repository Poisson-game certificate template, does not identify the geometry-specific marked experiment or validate its nuisance-aware observational transfer.
fill: The project instantiates finite-game certification for the disk and square Bernoulli-marked boundary experiments, proves that tangent information can matter, and supplies an observable nuisance-aware two-way transfer theorem, while keeping full unknown-density equivalence and global honesty separate from target-specific local-profile coverage.
